text:
By the time the second period was two minutes old, Nashville coach Andrew Brunette had seen enough of the Wild's top line to offer a verdict, as relayed by Heather Rule of NHL.com: "They might be the best line in the NHL. Best line I've seen so far this year. And they're rolling." Joel Eriksson Ek, Kirill Kaprizov and Matt Boldy combined for three goals and seven assists in a 7-3 rout, and Minnesota has now won four straight with points in 12 in a row.

The game was over in the first period. Brock Faber, in his second game back from a skull fracture, tipped in the opener at 4:20. Blake Coleman deflected in the second at 8:59, Maxim Shabanov beat Justus Annunen from distance on a 7% slap shot at 17:56, and Boldy made it 4-0 43 seconds later. Minnesota won the period 1.54 expected goals to 0.70 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and by the time Boldy's power-play goal made it 5-0 59 seconds into the second, Annunen's night was done. He allowed 3.7 more goals than his 20 shots deserved. Juuse Saros came on and stopped 17 of 18.

What followed was a strange, loose middle period with six goals. Nicolas Hague scored on a 1% chance for his 100th career point, Marcus Foligno answered 17 seconds later off a pass from his brother Nick, Jonathan Marchessault and Filip Forsberg pulled Nashville within 6-3, and Eriksson Ek tipped home the last goal with five seconds left in the period. Eriksson Ek finished with four points and Quinn Hughes logged 26:30 with two assists.

Over the whole game Minnesota had 3.88 expected goals to 2.54, and our replays give the Wild this one 71% of the time, so the score exaggerates the gap without inventing it. For Nashville, a seven-game winning streak that ended in San Jose has now turned into two straight losses, and this one came with a goalie question attached. For Minnesota, a team near the top of the West and still the focus of the Dylan Larkin talk, the top line is the strongest argument that it doesn't need anything at all.
headline: The Wild's top line runs Nashville out of the building
